issues.description: The template defines a function named create_y_state but the problem statement, tests, and the solution expect a function named make_y_state (with signature make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None). This name mismatch will cause student code based on the template to fail the tests (or confuse students), because calls and docstrings in the template refer to make_y_state while the actual implemented stub has a different name. For example, the problem tasks and template docstrings instruct implementing make_y_state, but the template only provides create_y_state (and its NotImplementedError message even refers to make_y_state), so students cannot implement the expected symbol without renaming.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the template stub create_y_state to make_y_state and ensure its signature matches the specification: def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None. Update any docstrings or internal references in the template to consistently use make_y_state so students and tests reference the same function name.

issues.description: The problem statement and tests ask students to implement a function named make_y_state(circ, q, p). However, the template repository defines a function named create_y_state(circ, q, p) (and its NotImplementedError message even refers to make_y_state). The solution repository implements make_y_state. This mismatch (create_y_state vs. make_y_state) is an unintended identifier naming inconsistency that will confuse students: they will look for make_y_state to implement or override, but the template exposes create_y_state, and automated tests / grading expect make_y_state.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the template identifier with the problem statement and solution. Rename the template function create_y_state to make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) and update its docstring/NotImplementedError message accordingly (or add a thin wrapper make_y_state that calls create_y_state). This ensures students and automated tests see the same function name to implement and matches the solution implementation.
